items.title: Direct (elective/procured) abortion
items.description: An AI use that facilitates, recommends, or carries out the direct termination of a pregnancy — e.g. an assistant that helps someone plan, obtain, or carry out an elective abortion, or a system that routes a user toward abortion as a recommended option. Not the same question as a system that discusses abortion informationally, or one whose users may raise it among many topics; this item is about the AI use itself directing toward or enabling the act.

citations.source: Compendium of the Social Doctrine of the Church
citations.reference: §155 (Ch. 3, §II, on the right to life as "the first among rights and the condition for all other rights of the person" — naming "the illicitness of every form of procured abortion and of euthanasia")

§55 (Ch. 2, within "The supreme value of human rights" — naming "induced abortion, killing of the innocent and euthanasia" as denials of the right to life "from conception to its natural end" that the Church considers gravely wrong)

items.title: Euthanasia or assisted suicide
items.description: An AI use that facilitates, recommends, or carries out ending a person's life at their own request or a caregiver's, including an assistant that helps plan or obtain the means for assisted suicide, or a system that recommends withdrawing ordinary care with the intent of causing death rather than allowing it.

citations.source: Compendium of the Social Doctrine of the Church

items.title: Direct, intentional killing of an innocent person
items.description: An AI use whose function is to identify, target, or cause the direct killing of a person who has done nothing to forfeit the right to life — the general case the two items above are specific instances of, and the tradition's own root case for this item: CCC 1867's "blood of Abel," the first of the sins that cry to heaven. Covers uses outside those two categories: e.g. an autonomous system designed to select and kill a specific non-combatant, or an assistant that helps plan such an act.

citations.source: Compendium of the Social Doctrine of the Church

items.title: Systemic denial of a worker's due wages, by design
items.description: An AI use whose function is to calculate, process, withhold, or report wages in a way designed to systematically deprive workers of wages they are legally and morally owed — e.g. a payroll or scheduling system built to under-report hours worked, misclassify workers to avoid wage obligations, or silently claw back earned pay, where the underpayment is the system's intended effect rather than an incidental bug or a good-faith dispute about how a contract or law applies. Not the same question as a payroll system that has an ordinary error rate, or one whose outputs are contested through a legitimate wage dispute — this item is about the AI use itself being built to produce the underpayment.

citations.reference: §1867 (Part Three, Section One, Chapter One, Article 8, §V "The Proliferation of Sin" — naming "injustice to the wage earner" among the "sins that cry to heaven")

§3 (quoting Gaudium et Spes §27 verbatim — naming "disgraceful working conditions, where people are treated as mere instruments of gain rather than as free and responsible persons" among the "infamies" the passage says "poison human society")

citations.source: Compendium of the Social Doctrine of the Church
citations.reference: §302 (Ch. 6, "Human Work" — "they commit grave injustice who refuse to pay a just wage or who do not give it in due time and in proportion to the work done"; "natural justice precedes and is above the freedom of the contract")

items.title: Facilitation of human trafficking or sexual exploitation
items.description:
An AI use that facilitates, recommends, or carries out human trafficking or the sexual exploitation of a person — e.g. a system that helps identify, recruit, transport, or advertise a person for trafficking or sexual exploitation, or that generates or distributes child sexual abuse material. Not the same question as a general-purpose system a user could misuse for this, or one that discusses the subject informationally (e.g. in a safety, legal, or support context); this item is about the AI use itself directing toward or enabling the act.
Note on citations: this item's Catechism grounding is CCC 1867's traditional association of "the sin of the Sodomites" with the sins that cry to heaven — an association this project treats cautiously given the narrative's own more expansive reading (Genesis 19, Ezekiel 16:49-50) as violent exploitation of the vulnerable, not a general judgment on a class of persons. The description above is written to what both readings agree is gravely wrong, not the contested part. See ../docs/ccc-citation-map.md and ../CHECKLIST.md, which flags this as the one item in this file without a clean, uncontested translation into an AI-use bright line.

citations.reference: §3 (quoting Gaudium et Spes §27 verbatim — naming "the selling of women and children" and "prostitution" among the "infamies" the passage says "poison human society")

§1867 (Part Three, Section One, Chapter One, Article 8, §V "The Proliferation of Sin" — naming "the sin of the Sodomites" among the "sins that cry to heaven"; see the note in this item's description above on how this project reads that association)
